Definition: to peck at, i.e. (figuratively) stun or dull
BiblicalUsage: Patsar means to press, to urge, to peck at, to stun. Lot presses the angels greatly in Genesis 19:3 until they turn in to his house, and Jacob urges Esau in Genesis 33:11 until he takes the present. The men of Gibeah press the old man in Judges 19:7, and he brings his concubine out to them.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that pressing can be hospitality or violence, and these three verses show both, yet the word is the same and the heart is what differs.
